AL.reason: The corpus contains Alabama Code Chapter 34-2 which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture, including definitions, registration requirements, the State Board for Registration of Architects, disciplinary provisions, and penalties.

AR.reason: The corpus contains the Arkansas Architectural Act (Chapter 17-15) which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in Arkansas, including definitions, board composition, examination requirements, registration, and enforcement.

AZ.reason: The corpus contains Arizona Title 32 Chapter on technical registration which explicitly covers architect registration requirements including qualifications, examinations, and board oversight for architects.

CA.reason: The corpus is California Business and Professions Code Chapter 3 (the Architects Practice Act), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in California.

CO.reason: Article 120 explicitly covers licensure of architects (Part 4, sections 12-120-401 through 12-120-417) along with engineers and surveyors, and the board created is specifically named the state board of licensure for architects, professional engineers, and professional land surveyors.

CT.reason: The corpus contains Connecticut's architect licensure chapter (Secs. 20-288 through 20-298c), including definitions, the Architectural Licensing Board, examination requirements, license renewal, suspension/revocation, and exemptions specifically governing the practice of architecture.

DE.reason: The corpus contains the full Delaware Board of Architects licensure chapter (§§ 301-317), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture.

FL.reason: The corpus is Florida Chapter 481 which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture and architects in Florida, including examination, licensure, disciplinary proceedings, and prohibitions.

GA.reason: The corpus is Georgia Title 43 Chapter 4 which directly establishes the licensing requirements, board, examinations, registration, and enforcement for architects in Georgia.

IA.reason: The corpus is Iowa Code Chapter 544A (Licensed Architects), which directly establishes the architectural examining board, sets licensure requirements, defines the practice of architecture, and regulates architects in Iowa.

ID.reason: The corpus contains Idaho Code Chapter 3 of Title 54, the Idaho Architecture Practice Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in Idaho.

IL.reason: The corpus is the Illinois Architecture Practice Act of 1989 (225 ILCS 305), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in Illinois.

IN.reason: The corpus is Indiana Title 25 Article 4 which directly licenses and regulates architects, covering board creation, registration requirements, examinations, fees, renewal, and practice definitions.

KY.reason: The corpus is Kentucky Chapter 323 (Architects), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in Kentucky, including definitions, license requirements, qualifications, fees, renewal, and disciplinary provisions.

LA.reason: The corpus contains Louisiana RS 37:141 through 37:158, which is the full Architecture licensure chapter establishing the State Board of Architectural Examiners, registration requirements, examinations, fees, and disciplinary provisions for architects in Louisiana.

MA.reason: The corpus contains the full Massachusetts architect licensure law including registration requirements, renewal, seal, discipline, and enforcement provisions under sections 60B through 60O.

MD.reason: The corpus contains Maryland Code GBO Title 3, which is the Maryland Architects Act, directly licensing and regulating the practice of architecture including definitions, board composition, examination, licensure, renewal, and discipline.

ME.reason: The corpus is Maine Title 32 Chapter 3-A which directly licenses architects (and landscape architects and interior designers), including licensing requirements, examinations, fees, and disciplinary provisions for architects.

MO.reason: Chapter 327 explicitly licenses architects in Missouri, defining the practice of architecture, establishing the licensing board, setting qualifications, examination, and renewal requirements for architects.

MS.reason: The corpus is Mississippi Code Title 73 Chapter 1, which is the state architecture licensing law establishing the State Board of Architecture, defining architect, and governing registration, examination, discipline, and renewal of architect certificates.

MT.reason: MCA Title 37 Chapter 65 is Montana's architecture licensure law, directly regulating the practice of architecture, defining architects, requiring licenses, and establishing the board of architects.

NC.reason: Chapter 83A contains the full licensure law for architects in North Carolina, including definitions, board composition, qualifications, examinations, fees, prohibited practice, and disciplinary procedures.

ND.reason: Chapter 43-03 explicitly establishes the registration requirements, board, examinations, fees, and disciplinary provisions for architects (and landscape architects) in North Dakota.

NJ.reason: The corpus contains the NJ State Board of Architects statutes (45:3-1 through 45:3-26) that directly establish and regulate the licensing of architects in New Jersey.

NM.reason: The corpus is New Mexico Chapter 61 Article 15, the Architectural Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in New Mexico.

NV.reason: The corpus is NRS Chapter 623, which directly licenses and regulates architects, residential designers, and registered interior designers in Nevada.

NY.reason: The corpus contains New York Education Law Article 147 sections 7300-7308 which directly define, license, and regulate the practice of architecture in New York.

OH.reason: The corpus contains Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4703 sections 4703.01 through 4703.19 which directly establish and regulate the licensure and practice of architecture in Ohio.

OK.reason: The corpus contains the State Architectural and Licensed Interior Designers Act (Title 59, §46.1 et seq.) which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in Oklahoma.

OR.reason: ORS chapter 671 sections 671.010 through 671.220 explicitly define and regulate the practice of architecture, including registration of architects and architectural firms in Oregon.

PA.reason: The corpus is the Pennsylvania Architects Licensure Law, directly licensing architects through examination, reciprocity, firm registration, and related provisions.

RI.reason: The corpus is Rhode Island General Laws Chapter 5-1, which is the dedicated licensure statute for architects, covering definitions, board establishment, examination, registration, fees, and discipline.

SC.reason: The corpus is SC Title 40 Chapter 3 which directly establishes the Board of Architectural Examiners, defines the practice of architecture, and sets licensure requirements for architects in South Carolina.

TX.reason: Chapter 1051 explicitly covers the Texas Board of Architectural Examiners and includes subchapters on registration of architects, board powers for architects, and disciplinary procedures for architects, which is the licensure law for architects in Texas.

UT.reason: The corpus is Utah Code Chapter 58-3a, the Architects Licensing Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of architecture in Utah.

VA.reason: The corpus contains Virginia Code Chapter 4 of Title 54.1 which explicitly defines architect, establishes the Board, sets licensure requirements, and regulates the practice of architecture in Virginia.

VT.reason: The corpus contains Vermont Title 26 Chapter 3 which directly licenses and regulates architects, including definitions, qualifications, board creation, license requirements, fees, and unprofessional conduct.

WA.reason: The corpus contains Washington RCW chapter 18.08, which is the architect licensing statute, covering registration requirements, the board for architects, examinations, certificates, and disciplinary provisions.

WI.reason: Chapter 443 explicitly contains registration requirements for architects (s. 443.03), examination requirements (s. 443.09), and related provisions governing the practice of architecture in Wisconsin.

WV.reason: Chapter 30-12 contains the full West Virginia licensure law for architects, including board composition, definitions, registration requirements, fees, seals, disciplinary procedures, and penalties.

WY.reason: The corpus contains Wyoming Title 33 Chapter 4 (W.S. 33-4-101 through 33-4-117), which is the direct licensure law for architects and landscape architects in Wyoming.
